body:
This check seems a bit fragile since there is no guarantee the caller will provide a `p_language` that corresponds to what `p_script_instance` is an instance of...

Can we instead use `ScriptInstance::get_language` ?
```c++
ERR_FAIL_COND(script->get_language() != script_instance->get_language());
```

(The added benefit would be to simply the API by being able to remove the `p_language` parameter entirely ^^)

Is there a reason we pass `p_script` instead of relying on `script_instance->get_script()` ?

According to `Object::set_script_and_instance`,  `p_script` and `p_script_instance` are not allowed to be `NULL`:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/eee39f004b42a4948af90cdebedf65c34a4a4970/core/object/object.cpp#L951-L955

So having `p_script` parameter only allows us to have `p_script != p_script_instance->get_script()` which I fail to see any benefit of having :thinking:

And besides, don't we want to just do `ERR_FAIL_COND(o->get_script() != script_instance->get_script())` instead ?

(I suspect it is not what we want since `Object::set_script_instance` do in fact overwrite `this->script` with `p_instance->get_script()`... however it's seems a bit odd given the naming suggests only `set_script_and_instance` should be able to change the script type :thinking: )

body: It would be helpful to explain the difference between `object_set_script_instance` and `object_set_script_and_instance` since they seems to do very similar behavior (see my previous comments ^^)

Thanks for the feedback!

The `p_language` parameter was meant to be for validating that the script on the object is using the language you think it is, which mirrors a similar check in `object_get_script_instance()`.

However, I didn't initially notice this:

> I suspect it is not what we want since Object::set_script_instance do in fact overwrite this->script with p_instance->get_script()

So, actually, there is no need to validate this! On setting the script instance, it'll also set the script.

That makes me wonder why `Object::set_script_and_instance()` even exists!
Yeah, based on the discussion above, I don't think we need `object_set_script_and_instance`
